s1.syndrome_frame: Acute metabolic crisis with renal failure in a patient with multiple comorbidities
key_facts: Decreased oral intake and dehydration for at least one week
Received 1 L of intravenous normal saline
Somnolent and oriented only to self
Vital signs: temperature 37.1 °C, blood pressure 101/59 mmHg, heart rate 105 beats per minute, respiratory rate 17 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation 100% on room air
Sarcopenic-appearing man with dry mucous membranes
Acute renal failure and severe metabolic acidosis
Sodium 145 mEq/L, potassium 6.6 mEq/L, blood urea nitrogen 207 mg/dL, creatinine 10.2 mg/dL
High-sensitivity troponin levels 213 ng/L at baseline, 223 ng/L at 1 hour, and 193 ng/L at 3 hours

differentials: Ketoacidosis due to type 2 diabetes mellitus
Ketosis due to medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency
per_call: Ketoacidosis due to type 2 diabetes mellitus
Ketosis due to medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency

shortlist.label: Euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus and presents with severe metabolic acidosis, elevated β-hydroxybutyrate level, and glucose level of 185 mg/dL

shortlist.label: Lactic acidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has severe metabolic acidosis, elevated lactate level of 4.4 mmol/L, and clinical signs of poor perfusion

shortlist.label: Uremic acidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has acute renal failure with elevated creatinine level of 10.2 mg/dL and severe metabolic acidosis

shortlist.label: Starvation ketosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of decreased oral intake and dehydration for at least one week, which could contribute to ketosis

shortlist.label: Acute tubular necrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has acute renal failure with elevated creatinine level of 10.2 mg/dL, which could be caused by acute tubular necrosis

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, decreased oral intake and dehydration, acute renal failure, severe metabolic acidosis, and an elevated β-hydroxybutyrate level, which are all consistent with euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis, especially given the recent initiation of empagliflozin, a medication known to increase the risk of euDKA.

rejected.label: Lactic acidosis
rejected.why: While the patient has an elevated lactate level, the presence of ketones and the clinical context suggest euDKA as a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Uremic acidosis
rejected.why: Although the patient has acute renal failure, the presence of ketones and the recent initiation of empagliflozin point more towards euDKA.

rejected.label: Starvation ketosis
rejected.why: While the patient had decreased oral intake, the presence of severe metabolic acidosis and an elevated β-hydroxybutyrate level in the context of diabetes and empagliflozin use suggests euDKA.

rejected.label: Acute tubular necrosis
rejected.why: This diagnosis does not fully explain the metabolic acidosis and ketosis observed in the patient.
